title: Deterministic Verification with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent; that identical candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Note: the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand and inference apply to the synthetic/emulation partition only. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are actively explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior surveys and empirical work document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. Such pipelines reduce mechanically checkable error classes (syntax, ordering, local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of validator-and-repair guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal effect of a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). The confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline measured on a synthetic/emulation partition of N_pairs = 250 intents. Our contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (with exact counts, CIs, and adapter-level reconciliation) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps and LLM literature motivates GVR architectures and emphasizes the need for deterministic checks. Studies of LLMs applied to intent-to-configuration tasks report usable draft configurations under controlled conditions but note residual syntax/semantic errors and the need for verification layers [1],[2]. Empirical and methodological work in configuration and program repair shows generate-then-verify workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects [4],[5]. Deterministic verification and model-checking tools (header-space analysis, Batfish, Plankton, etc.) are mature approaches for reachability and policy checks and are commonly integrated as validators in such pipelines [3],[6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection highlight retrieval/tooling threats to agentic pipelines and motivate filtering and validation layers, but adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational risk [7].

This study differs by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting reconciled provider-call accounting and stage_counts so readers can audit initial-generation vs repair usage, and (iii) archiving deterministic validator traces and analysis artifacts for reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1. The confirmatory design specified N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, a single permitted automated repair per episode, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Analysis methods were frozen: exact two-sided McNemar for paired outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is recorded in the evidence bundle (see Disclosure).

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intents. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (make-before-break, must-be-down rules, protected interfaces). Tasks exercised a range of difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard) and common NetOps workflow patterns. The full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting (explicit paragraph requested by reviewers). Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced by the declared model (gpt-5-mini) per intent; that identical generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded). The preregistered policy permitted up to one deterministic template-driven repair per episode if the validator failed; no independent first-pass generation was performed per condition. Provider-call accounting from the adapter reconciles to model_calls_used = 251, decomposed into 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call. For clarity: the adapter's stage_counts record per-stage activity (shared_initial_generation = 250; repair = 1) and condition_counts reflect how the adapter labels shared-generation vs repair events; these mappings are reconciled in the archived deterministic reconciliation artifact so the reader can verify that exactly one initial generation per intent was reused across conditions.

LLM invocation and guardrail pipeline. All initial generations used the declared model gpt-5-mini (model_configuration recorded in the evidence bundle). The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, counting parsed_command_count, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow constraints, and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the task's expected_final_state. If validation failed in a guarded episode, the pipeline permitted a single deterministic repair attempt constrained to syntactic and ordering fixes (reorder commands to match required_sequence, split/join lines, correct token ordering) and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration repairs or free-form LLM re-generation were allowed in the confirmatory run.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items failing deterministic vendor-parsers that prevented verification and items flagged for credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from the primary analysis. The registered missingness plan specified deterministic retry policies for API failures and sensitivity analyses treating excluded/incomplete pairs as failures. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged; complete_pair_count = 250.
sections.results:
Execution and counts. Execution completed the confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. The adapter-stage reconciliation shows shared_initial_generation = 250 and repair = 1. Primary binary outcomes (validator-scored success): baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency table is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0–1.2 percentage points). The single discordant pair was converted from baseline-fail to guarded-pass by the single permitted repair; the repair-conversion rate observed on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.4%.

Representative validator diagnostics. Validator traces for passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count and valid = true. Representative artifacts (shared responses, normalized configurations, and validator traces) are archived; a typical hard-difficulty task (example task-000003) shows parsed_command_count = 6 and required_command_count = 6 with valid = true in both episodes.

Missingness and contamination. No episodes were excluded, and contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes. Analysis CSVs and the paired contingency table are archived in the evidence bundle for audit.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational meaning. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained emulation-style task bank used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases; the single exercised repair converted the sole failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these study conditions.

Why the observed marginal gain is small. Artifact-grounded factors explain the near-null effect: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and strict allowed_touched_fields that reduced task ambiguity; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) but does not capture richer semantic correctness in live protocol execution or emergent cross-device interactions.

Power and assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) substantially exceeded that assumption, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements; therefore the paired-bootstrap CI that bounds the possible improvement is the most informative confirmatory output.

Threats to validity. Internal: outcomes depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the particular validator encoding. Construct: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness and does not assert behavioral correctness in live execution. External: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; community and production-like partitions were not executed. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.

Framing for practice. These results indicate that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This finding does not imply validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts; validator scope, production heterogeneity, multi-iteration repairs, and human escalation can materially change operational utility.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intents, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced herein are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: after an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review and revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and key artifacts: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Primary archived execution manifest and analysis artifacts are available in the evidence bundle; key manifest pointer for reproduction: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9). The confirmatory estimand reported in this paper (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) was evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only; the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, expected_final_state) but did not measure behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or emergent cross-device effects.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
